findings.excerpt_quote: Business goal is to enable user to add all the children and children of children (etc) of selected work items to the scope of box.
findings.finding_summary: The Acceptance Criteria field is empty on the Epic and on all three children, and no description holds AC bullets. The epic has a one-line goal and no testable completion criterion.
findings.testing_impact: No epic-level acceptance test can be defined; pass criteria have to come from each child's own scan.
findings.question_for_PM: What observable outcome marks this epic done?

findings.finding_summary: Nothing states whether "recurringly" means the box keeps following the hierarchy after the scope is saved. ONE-356784 persists a flag on the scope definition, but no source says whether descendants that are added, removed or re-parented later join or leave the box on the next refresh, or only the tree present at save time counts. The Structure screenshot shows a "Choose type of extend rule" dialog, but its layout is not a rule for BigPicture.
findings.testing_impact: The core state transition (hierarchy changes after save) has no expected result, so neither a one-time nor a live-rule test can be written.
findings.question_for_PM: Does the box follow later hierarchy changes, or only the tree present when the scope is saved?

findings.excerpt_quote: Create box work items structure using recurring issue links
findings.finding_summary: The sources disagree on which relationship is traversed. The epic summary and linked Idea PPMR-342 say "recurring issue links"; the customer quote in ONE-36236 says issues are linked "via normal issue linking"; the Structure example offers both "Child Work Items" and "Linked Items". Yet ONE-36236 strikes through the "other Jira link" option, leaving only the Parent field. The epic never states that link-based traversal is out of scope.
findings.testing_impact: QA cannot tell whether issue-link hierarchies are in the test matrix or are an expected non-feature.
findings.question_for_PM: Is traversal by Jira issue links in scope, or only the Parent field?

findings.excerpt_quote: When defining the scope, the user also has the option to enter Key IDs for multiple tasks.
findings.finding_summary: The children describe two different user interactions. ONE-36236 has the user enter task keys, with structure builders adjusted automatically. ONE-350189 adds one toggle below "Refresh search list", and ONE-356784 stores one boolean for the whole scope definition. No source says whether the toggle applies only to entered keys or also to projects, boards and filters in the same scope, or how it combines with Narrow Down.
findings.testing_impact: The primary flow cannot be written end to end: the inputs the toggle acts on are undefined.
findings.question_for_PM: What does the toggle act on, and how does it relate to key entry?

findings.excerpt_quote: [BE] Confirm if ONE-324524 have impact on ScopeDef refactor
findings.finding_summary: The spike opened to check this epic's impact on the Scope Def data-storage refactor (ONE-357566) is Canceled, and the related refactor epic ONE-235869 is still Open. No outcome is recorded on this epic, so "no impact" is an unstated assumption.
findings.testing_impact: Regression scope for the persisted flag is unknown if ONE-235869 later changes how scope definitions are stored.
findings.question_for_PM: Was the impact on the Scope Def refactor confirmed elsewhere?

findings.excerpt_quote: Parent link (determination of descendant tasks will be done based on the Jira Cloud “parent” field or “parent” field + “parent-link” + ”epic-link” for DC.
findings.finding_summary: The Jira edition matrix is unsettled. ONE-36236 specifies Data Center behaviour and DC structure builders; the linked Confluence analysis says the DC variant is probably not worth implementing for performance reasons; the epic's Host platform field lists only Atlassian Cloud. The same page lists different query options for Cloud Standard, Cloud Premium and team-managed projects, and no child says which are supported.
findings.testing_impact: The environment matrix (DC, Cloud Standard, Cloud Premium, team-managed) cannot be fixed, which sets how many configurations need a pass.
findings.question_for_PM: Which Jira editions and project types are supported?

findings.excerpt_quote: This change will have a negative impact on performance
findings.finding_summary: No depth limit, item-count limit or time target is stated for building the descendant tree. ONE-36236 acknowledges a negative performance impact, and the Confluence analysis lists a criterion requiring the user to also enter a project to narrow the search, but ONE-36236 does not carry that criterion forward.
findings.testing_impact: Boundary and large-hierarchy tests have no pass threshold.
findings.question_for_PM: Is there a depth, size or time limit, and is a project selection required?

findings.excerpt_quote: When defining the scope, the user also has the option to enter Key IDs for multiple tasks.
findings.finding_summary: No behaviour is stated for an entered key that doesn't exist, is mistyped, or points to an issue the user cannot browse.
findings.testing_impact: Negative-path tests for key entry have no expected result.

findings.excerpt_quote: Business goal is to enable user to add all the children and children of children (etc) of selected work items to the scope of box.
findings.finding_summary: No source says who may enable the toggle, or what happens to descendants the box's scope context user cannot see in Jira.
findings.testing_impact: Role and visibility tests cannot be scoped.

findings.finding_summary: The child status mix rules out an epic-level end-to-end pass for now. The toggle (ONE-350189) and flag persistence (ONE-356784) are Waiting for Release, but the query change that actually uses the flag (ONE-36236) is still In Progress.
findings.testing_impact: An end-to-end check (toggle on, scope built with descendants) waits until ONE-36236 is delivered.

findings.finding_summary: A feature flag is named only on the front-end child ONE-350189, with status DISABLED. The epic's own flag fields are empty, nobody is named as owner of switching it on, and no source says whether the same flag also controls the back-end query change in ONE-36236.
findings.testing_impact: QA cannot plan flag-on and flag-off coverage or know when the feature becomes testable in a shared environment.
findings.question_for_PM: Who switches the flag on, when, and does it cover the back-end change too?

report.readiness_line: The epic has no acceptance criteria, and its children leave open what "recurringly" means after save and which relationships are traversed (RR-ONE-324524-01, RR-ONE-324524-03; Q1, Q2).

facts.text: Epic goal: "Business goal is to enable user to add all the children and children of children (etc) of selected work items to the scope of box."

The Epic description's only illustration, captioned "Example from Structure", shows a dialog titled "Create Extend Generator" with the prompt "Choose type of extend rule:" and two options: "Child Work Items — Pull in child work items using the Parent field." and "Linked Items — Pull in work items that are linked to work items already in the structure."

ONE-36236: the user can enter Key IDs for multiple tasks; BigPicture adds those tasks and "all descendants of these tasks to the scope (the whole tree)", adjusts structure builders, and the result can be combined with projects, boards and filters and narrowed with Narrow Down.
ONE-36236 strikes through the option "other Jira link (user can select 1 link - determination of descendant tasks will be done based on that link)"; the remaining option is the Parent link.
ONE-36236 states "This change will have a negative impact on performance".

ONE-350189: a new toggle on the scopeDefinition module below "Refresh search list", described as "Include all children recurringly"; the flag is passed in area/task/scope/def/update and persisted in the database.
ONE-350189 carries feature flag ScopeDefinitionIncludeAllChildrenRecurringly with status DISABLED; the epic's own flag fields are empty.
facts.source: ONE-350189 FF Name / FF Status fields

facts.text: ONE-356784: includeAllChildrenRecurringly has default value False, is stored as a boolean, and is added to the scope definition DTO.

The Confluence analysis compares Parent-field and Jira-link approaches across Cloud Standard, Cloud Premium and Data Center, notes that team-managed projects lack some queries, and says the Data Center variant is probably not worth implementing for performance reasons (Cloud only).
facts.source: Confluence — Scope definition based on parents keys, appfireteam.atlassian.net

facts.text: Epic Host platform: Atlassian Cloud. UX Design status: To decide. Figma (URL): empty.

not_stated: Acceptance criteria for the epic or any child.
Whether the box follows hierarchy changes made after the scope is saved.
An explicit out-of-scope note for issue-link traversal, which the epic summary still names.
Error handling for scope builds that time out or fail (B4).
Test data or environment for multi-level hierarchies, including which Jira edition is used (B10).
Logging or audit of scope changes made through this feature (B11).
A design reference for the toggle: UX Design status is 'To decide' and the Figma field is empty.

risks.text: The mechanism acts on box scope definitions, which every box uses; with no stated performance threshold and an acknowledged negative impact, large hierarchies are the main regression risk.
If link-based traversal is out of scope, the customer case quoted in ONE-36236 (issues linked "via normal issue linking") is not served, which may surface late as a scope dispute.
A canceled impact spike next to an open refactor of the same data storage leaves the persisted flag exposed to a later storage change.

testing_focus.text: Once Q1 is answered, test a hierarchy change after save (add, remove and re-parent a descendant) and check box scope on the next refresh.
Combine key entry and the toggle with a project, board or filter source and with Narrow Down, to confirm what the toggle acts on.
Run a large and deep hierarchy against a stated time or size limit.
Cover both flag states for ScopeDefinitionIncludeAllChildrenRecurringly, and the default False on existing boxes.
One end-to-end pass (toggle on, save, scope built with descendants) after ONE-36236 is delivered.
